title: Evening debug blitz: async-prefill & kernel race notes
content:
Context:
Quick evening notes from a small-focus session to triage an uptick in 95th/99th tail latency for short-chat requests (seq <= 128) observed across a handful of customers. This doc is a working journal: logs, experiments, decisions, and next steps. It intentionally mixes raw observations and formatted action items so we can ingest into the postmortem later.

Summary (top-line):
- Root cause hypothesis at the end of the session: an edge-case race between async prefill coalescing and the new micro-kernel swap that leaves some requests queued without KV warmup, causing expensive cold KV reads plus an unanticipated serialization path in the kernel.
- Impact: transient p95 increase from ~80ms -> ~340ms for affected tenants during bursts; sustained p50 unchanged. Affected ~0.8% of production traffic during a 18:30–19:15 window on 2026-08-18.
- Short-term mitigation deployed (19:05): revert micro-kernel swap for legacy kernel ABI on the node pool with prefilling enabled (hotfix), restoring p95 to ~95ms.

Timeline and standup-style log (timestamps UTC):
- 18:12 — Automated alert (observability) flagged concurrent p95 jumps for model rwd-llama-compat-7b on eu-west-1.
- 18:15 — On-call SRE (Riley) posted initial traces in Slack; patterns show 3x increase in full KV fetches during prefill window.
- 18:22 — Small triage huddle (Marco, Asha, Riley) — hypothesized race with async prefill coalescer after kernel patch (PR 987) switched to eager packing.
- 18:28 — Captured flamegraphs + per-request trace: cold KV fetch + kernel fallback path executing scalar fallback for same request. See trace ids: trace-8375, trace-8376.
- 18:35 — Priya runs repro load in staging with synthetic short-chat traces; confirms increased latency when kernel swap enabled and prefill coalescing threshold low.
- 18:50 — Experiment 1: bump prefill coalescing window from 6ms -> 12ms in staging: p95 improves modestly.
- 18:58 — Experiment 2: enable KV optimistic warmup (best-effort prefix replay) in staging; p95 drops near baseline but increased tail variance observed on high-concurrency jobs.
- 19:05 — Hotfix toggle: revert kernel swap on affected node pool -> production p95 back to acceptable range; rollback checklist executed.
- 19:12 — Post-hotfix observation: no error increase; reduced CPU contention observed on nodes; planners assigned follow-ups.

Technical observations (raw):
- Repro in staging used: short-chat harness with concurrency 60, median sequence 64, endpoints hitting rwd-llama-compat-7b. The specific workload that regressed is prefix-heavy (many repeated opens).
- Kernel change (PR 987) introduced an eager-buffer packing optimization that assumes KV cache state will be warm by the time the kernel runs. When async-prefill coalescer defers warmup for very short gaps (<10ms) the kernel sometimes falls back to a slower path that traverses an alternative tokenizer alignment code path.
- The expensive path includes an extra memcpy + token remap + fallback attention mask recalculation that adds ~220–280ms in the observed traces.
- KV cache eviction heuristic (LFU decay) had a corner where very short-lived entries were being evicted before they could be reused under bursty parallelism.

Experiments run (brief results):
- Stage A: increase coalescing window 6 -> 12 ms. Result: p95 reduced by ~40% vs regressed baseline, p50 unchanged. Effective for low-burst traffic, but increased latency for medium-length sequences under very high concurrency.
- Stage B: optimistic KV warmup toggle (best-effort async prefix fetch). Result: tail latency drops to near baseline, but CPU spikes on prefill workers increased by ~15% and memory pressure rose on some nodes.
- Stage C: kernel no-eager-packing compile (branchless fallback avoided). Result: no tail regression but throughput dropped by ~6% for long sequences; not acceptable for general rollout.

Decisions made in-session:
- Immediate: Roll back micro-kernel swap for node pool with prefilling enabled (hotfix applied). Rationale: restore stable SLAs quickly; hotfix has low blast radius.
- Near-term (next 72h): implement a guard in the kernel that detects cold-KV path and forces a short blocking warmup if the prefill state is unavailable (triage flag gated). This should avoid the expensive fallback without reverting packing totally.
- Medium-term (2–3 weeks): revisit KV eviction decay constants and add a short-lived reservation slot for recently-prefetched keys to reduce churn during bursts.

Open action items (owner | ETA):
- Add guard in kernel to detect missing KV and trigger short blocking warmup | Marco Nguyen | 2026-08-21
- Run a controlled A/B rollout for guard across 10% of nodes in eu-west-1 | Riley Chen | 2026-08-22
- Tweak LFU decay and reservation slot simulation in perf harness; publish results | Priya Singh | 2026-08-24
- Create synthetic tenant workload that captures prefix-heavy short-chat to include in nightly regression suite | Asha Patel | 2026-08-20
- Update observability dashboards to split prefill vs kernel fallback latency components | Diego Morales | 2026-08-21

Notes for postmortem draft (items to capture):
- Exact sequence of events: alert -> traces -> diagnostics -> rollback (times + owners).
- Quantify customer impact (list tenants, traffic %), include customer outreach drafts and CS handoff.
- Attach key traces (trace-8375, trace-8376) and flamegraphs.
- Link to PRs and feature flags involved: PR 987, FF:prefill-async-v2, FF:kernel-eager-pack.

Mini-retrospective / learnings:
- Pushing micro-optimizations (kernel packing) without explicit prefill contract assumptions is risky; we need a test harness that simulates missy prefill windows across kernel transitions.
- Observability: we need clearer telemetry on when kernel falls back to alternate code paths (add a counter + tag).
- Ops: feature-flagged kernel rollouts should monitor a special prefill-sensitivity metric to auto-rollback if tail increases >2x baseline.

Appendix: useful links and quick debug commands used during session
- Perf harness: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-harness/tree/prefill-tests
- Repro command (staging): ./run_prefill_harness --concurrency 60 --seq-dist short --model rwd-llama-compat-7b --trace-output /tmp/stage-trace-aug18.json
- Flamegraph script: /bin/produce-flame.sh /tmp/stage-trace-aug18.json
- Slack thread: #runtime-debugging/thread-az3k (search for ‘overnight prefill tail’).

Quick notes to self (loose ideas to investigate):
- Could we provide a lightweight per-request prefill affinity token so kernels know to expect warm KV?
- Is there a way to shadow kernel eager-packing in user space to validate assumptions before swapping binary?
- Consider pre-allocating a tiny warm slot in KV for very recent prefixes to avoid LFU churn.

If you're reading this and want to help: ping me (Asha) with any extra traces or if you can run the simulation locally. I'll assemble the postmortem skeleton tomorrow morning and assign the customer comms draft to CS.

-- end of session log (Asha Patel, 2026-08-19 07:08 UTC)
